name: Oura
tagline: A finger-worn sensor ring plus a subscription app that scores your sleep, readiness and activity.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The app is the cheap half. The expensive half is a titanium ring with infrared PPG, skin temperature and accelerometer sensors on your finger, plus years of validation work turning those raw signals into sleep staging and an HRV baseline that means something. An agent can absolutely build you a dashboard, a scoring formula and a trend chart in an afternoon; it cannot build the thing that measures you while you are unconscious. If you already own another wearable that exports data, a personal replacement for the app layer is real and useful. If you are trying to replace the ring, the answer is buy a sensor, not write code.
coreLoopDIY: A local dashboard that ingests sleep and heart rate data from an existing wearable export, computes your own readiness score against a rolling personal baseline, and charts trends.
requirements: An actual sensor source: Apple Health / Google Fit export, or a wearable with a data export or API
Some patience with messy health export formats
At least two weeks of history before any baseline score is meaningful
whatYouLose: Continuous overnight sensing from a device that does not need charging every day
Validated sleep staging, which is genuinely hard signal processing and not a heuristic you invent on Saturday
Skin temperature trends, illness and cycle detection built on that data
A polished mobile app with background sync, notifications and years of onboarding work
Longitudinal comparison against population data, which is the only reason a score of 78 means anything
moatNotes: The subscription is a rounding error next to the sensor package and the staging models trained against polysomnography.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the subscription is not really what you are buying. You bought a ring that quietly measures you for months without being asked, and the fee keeps the interpretation layer running on top of it. People pay because the alternative is either raw numbers with no meaning or a competing device with the same arrangement. The app is replaceable; the sensor on your finger and the model that turns its noise into sleep stages is not, at least not in one session.
notes: You can rebuild the scoreboard in an afternoon, but not the sensor that fills it. The moat is a validated hardware sensor on your finger plus the sleep staging models trained against clinical data.
prompt:
Build a local-only personal sleep and recovery dashboard. Stack: Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) with SQLite via better-sqlite3, Tailwind for styling, Recharts for charts. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry. It runs on localhost with `npm run dev` and stores everything in ./data/health.db.

This is NOT a replacement for a wearable. It assumes the user already has a sensor and can export data. Make that clear in the README.

Data in:
1. An importer for Apple Health export.zip: parse export.xml with a streaming XML parser, extract HKCategoryTypeIdentifierSleepAnalysis, HKQuantityTypeIdentifierHeartRate, HKQuantityTypeIdentifierHeartRateVariabilitySDNN, HKQuantityTypeIdentifierRestingHeartRate, HKQuantityTypeIdentifierStepCount. Handle files over 500MB without loading them into memory.
2. A CSV importer with a documented column format for people exporting from other devices.
3. A manual daily entry form: bedtime, wake time, subjective energy 1-5, notes, alcohol yes/no, late caffeine yes/no.

Derived layer:
- Nightly rollup table: total sleep, sleep efficiency, mid-sleep time, average overnight HR, HRV, resting HR.
- A readiness score 0-100 computed from z-scores of HRV, resting HR and sleep duration against a rolling 30-day personal baseline, weights defined in one config file and documented in the README. Do not pretend this is clinically validated. Label it "personal heuristic" in the UI.
- Do not attempt sleep stage classification. If the import has stages, display them; if not, say so.

UI: one dashboard page with a 90-day readiness line chart, a sleep duration bar chart, a correlation panel showing readiness against the boolean tags (alcohol, late caffeine), and a table of nightly rows with drill-down. One import page. One settings page for score weights.

Include seed data generation so the app looks alive before any real import. Write a README covering setup, the Apple Health export steps, the CSV format, and an explicit "what this is not" section.
